column1: # ledger-readers.tsv: every program under scripts/ that reads the ledger, asks, health, lanes, followUps, freeze or deployWindows,
# found by grep (scripts/test/field-reads.sh discovers them; a program not listed here fails the check, and a line that no
# longer matches the grep fails as stale). Columns (tab separated):
# kind: seam   the compiled jq program is dumped (CM_TEST seam) and every field NAME it reads is checked against its own inventory
#              (stall-fields.tsv, digest-fields.tsv, asktimeout-fields.tsv, and their read-allow lists)
#       scan   no seam: the source is scanned line by line for the protective fields below, and every read of standing, freeze, a
#              state with a default, issue or project, and worker must use the typed idiom or sit on protective-read-allow.tsv with a reason
#       none   reads the ledger only for display, timing, ids or a path: it holds no protective read (the note says why)
# protective fields = the fields whose wrong type must never erase a protection: standing (a lead is never cleaned up), state (an
# unknown state is never resumed), freeze (a garbled freeze is never read as off), issue and issueUrl (an escalation exists), project
# (the ledger belongs to this project), worker (a deploy window has an owner).
# States are matched exactly (cm_state_norm only maps a legacy spelling to its current word): deliberate, see SKILL.md.
